user_consequence: During round setup (new-round-client.tsx), the exact screen this hook exists to protect (poor-signal, on-course, offline-durability-critical), the device runs TWO independent 30-second polling loops: one owned by the dashboard-wide OfflineProvider, one owned by the round-setup screen itself. Each does its own fetch('/api/health', HEAD) with its own AbortController/timeout, its own online/offline/Network-Information change listeners, and its own React state.
mechanism: useConnectionStatus (src/hooks/golf/use-connection-status.ts) is a plain hook with per-call state — no module-level dedup, no context, no store. Called directly from OfflineProvider (src/components/golf/OfflineProvider.tsx:91), mounted once dashboard-wide by FairwayDashboardShell.tsx:726 wrapping children, and independently from new-round-client.tsx:155 inside that same children subtree during round setup. Both default to 30000ms (use-connection-status.ts:74). A third call site, OfflineSyncStatus.tsx:210-213 (60000ms), is currently dormant because the only OfflineProvider mount passes showSyncStatus={false}. The hook's periodic-check effect (use-connection-status.ts:277-306) never checks document.visibilityState, unlike the app's own reusable useVisibilityAwareInterval (src/hooks/useVisibilityAwareInterval.ts, unused here) and unlike sibling pollers in this codebase (notification-badge-context.tsx:228-231, useNotifications.ts:147-161) which do gate on visibility.
expected: One owner per recurring connectivity check, shared across every consumer via context/store/singleton, paused on backgrounding like sibling pollers already do in this codebase.
actual: Independent per-call-site timers/listeners with no visibility gating in the hook itself.
proposed_fix: Convert useConnectionStatus's connectivity-check loop into a module-level singleton (mirroring getSyncEngine()), or expose it through OfflineProvider's existing OfflineContext instead of re-calling the hook; route its interval through useVisibilityAwareInterval; delete the independent instantiation in new-round-client.tsx:155 in favor of context.
performance_check: RISK only — no device profile available this phase. Would need a release-build network panel during round setup showing two independent HEAD requests to /api/health on the same ~30s cadence.

user_consequence: A genuine stale-server-action failure during an active task can trigger TWO independent, uncoordinated recovery attempts instead of one bounded recovery coordinator. One path clears service-worker caches and unregisters the SW before reloading; the other shows a toast and reloads on a plain 250ms timer. Neither knows the other fired.
mechanism: StaleDeploymentRecoveryScript is an inline beforeInteractive <Script> injected into every page (src/components/providers/StaleDeploymentRecoveryScript.tsx, mounted unconditionally in src/app/layout.tsx). Its isStaleDeploymentError() (lines 30-45) matches message.includes('server action') && (message.includes('not found on the server') || message.includes('was not found')), and attaches window.addEventListener('error', ...) (line 152) and ('unhandledrejection', ...) (line 171), each calling reloadFresh() (lines 115-149), guarded by its own sessionStorage key 'chunk-error-reload' and URL param '__deployment_refresh' (lines 8-9). Independently, src/lib/error-logging.ts's isStaleServerActionError() (lines 152-169: /Server Action ".*" was not found on the server/.test(msg) || msg.includes('was not found on the server')) overlaps materially, and setupGlobalErrorHandlers() (lines 630-679, mounted via GlobalErrorHandlerSetup in the same root layout) attaches its own window 'unhandledrejection' (line 633) and 'error' (line 659) listeners, each calling softReloadForStaleServerAction() (lines 527-566) guarded by a DIFFERENT key, STALE_ACTION_RELOAD_KEY = 'stale-action-auto-reload' (line 508). The doc comment at error-logging.ts:499-506 explicitly states the intended invariant ('there must be exactly one source of truth, otherwise two paths can each first-reload the same session') and exports the key for other modules to coordinate on — the inline script does not. Neither error handler calls stopImmediatePropagation, so both fire for one qualifying event.
expected: One recovery coordinator per error class, one shared guard key/state machine (C09).
actual: Two independently authored classifiers with overlapping match conditions, two independent guard keys, both wired to the same global events.
proposed_fix: Either have StaleDeploymentRecoveryScript's inline classifier defer to softReloadForStaleServerAction/STALE_ACTION_RELOAD_KEY for the server-action-specific case, or have error-logging.ts check/honor the inline script's chunk-error-reload key first. Either leaves exactly one decision point.
performance_check: NOT_RUN — requires reproducing a real stale server-action error against a release build.

user_consequence: Opening Calendar starts a second independent notification poll on top of the one already running for the whole dashboard session, doubling notification-related network/render work while Calendar is open, for overlapping data the badge count already tracks.
mechanism: NotificationBadgeProvider (src/contexts/notification-badge-context.tsx) is mounted once dashboard-wide and polls every 45s (POLL_INTERVAL, line 59), visibility-gated (lines 228-231); its own comment (lines 29-36) states the design rule that NotificationBell should read this context 'instead of this provider adding a second poll loop for the same feed.' NotificationCenter (src/components/golf/calendar/NotificationCenter.tsx:107-110) instead calls useNotifications({limit:20, pollInterval:30000}) — a separate hook (src/hooks/useNotifications.ts) hitting a different server action (getNotifications) on its own 30s cadence. Mounted from PremiumCalendarClient.tsx at line 1161 (mobile) and line 1253 (desktop), mutually exclusive per render via isMobile but still a second live poll loop whenever Calendar is open. The comment at PremiumCalendarClient.tsx:1228-1237 confirms this is a known, unresolved stopgap ('until the shell-level consolidation lands — single instance app-wide').
expected: One poll owner per notification feed; Calendar's bell reads from NotificationBadgeProvider's context instead of independently polling.
actual: Two independent, differently-cadenced pollers for overlapping notification data whenever Calendar is open.
proposed_fix: Consolidate NotificationCenter onto NotificationBadgeProvider's context/counts instead of useNotifications' independent poll, or hoist a single NotificationCenter/bell instance into FairwayDashboardShell/FairwayTopBar as the code's own comment already proposes.
performance_check: NOT_RUN — device/network trace would need to show two independent fetch cadences while Calendar is open.

user_consequence: Every travel-expense CSV export leaks one blob URL (and its backing memory) for the rest of the tab's lifetime. Low-frequency, user-triggered, small payloads, but a real and easily-avoided leak that compounds across a long session (T23).
mechanism: handleExportCSV in src/components/fairway/pages/travel/FairwayTravel.tsx:296-310 calls URL.createObjectURL(blob) at line 304 to build a download link, appends/clicks/removes the anchor, but never calls URL.revokeObjectURL anywhere in the function or file (grepped: zero matches). The same codebase has the correct pattern elsewhere for the identical case — e.g. src/components/baseball/practice-planner/PracticePrintExport.tsx:129-132 (setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(blobUrl), 60_000)) and src/components/fairway/pages/documents/FairwayDocuments.tsx:676-683 — so this is a local omission, not a missing capability.
expected: Every createObjectURL call in a repeatable user action has a matching revokeObjectURL.
actual: No revoke call anywhere in the file for this blob URL.
proposed_fix: Add URL.revokeObjectURL(link.href) immediately after link.click() (or on a short setTimeout matching the PracticePrintExport.tsx pattern).
owner_lane: UNASSIGNED — Travel feature owner not named in Section 6; A00 to route
performance_check: RISK only — memory growth from repeated exports is plausible from source, not measured.

user_consequence: Every click across the app is eligible for PostHog's default autocapture, which can include the clicked element's visible text/attributes sent to PostHog's servers, with no code-level mask or opt-out configured — independent of whether full session-replay recording is separately enabled.
mechanism: src/components/providers/PostHogProvider.tsx:20-27 calls posthog.init(key, {api_host: host, capture_pageview: false, capture_pageleave: true, persistence: 'localStorage+cookie'}). It never sets autocapture:false nor any mask_all_text/mask_all_element_attributes/ph-no-capture policy. posthog-js's documented default is autocapture ON unless explicitly disabled. Contrast: Datadog RUM's init (src/lib/datadog/index.ts:46-63) sets defaultPrivacyLevel:'mask-user-input' alongside sessionReplaySampleRate:20 — a real privacy decision — but mask-user-input masks form-input VALUES only, not general on-screen text, so the same private-text-outside-an-input caveat applies there too, just with a partial existing mitigation PostHog lacks entirely. Whether PostHog session recording is separately toggled on for this project is a remote dashboard-side setting not visible from source.
expected: Session replay/autocapture explicitly masked/reviewed per Section 11.1, not switched on broadly with default config.
actual: PostHog init has no autocapture/masking configuration at all; Datadog has a partial one (input-only masking, not general text).
proposed_fix: Pass autocapture:false to posthog.init (manual event capture is already the stated intent), or configure mask_all_text:true / a dd-privacy-style opt-in mask convention. Consider whether Datadog's defaultPrivacyLevel should move from mask-user-input to mask given student-athlete data is involved. This is an owner privacy decision, not a unilateral code change; no new SDK proposed.

user_consequence: No direct user-facing consequence — recorded as a positive-contrast PASS finding that calibrates A11-001: the codebase already knows how to prevent the exact duplicate-timer problem A11-001 describes, which strengthens rather than weakens that finding since the fix pattern already exists in-repo.
mechanism: src/lib/offline/sync-engine.ts exports getSyncEngine() (lines 1271-1279) as a module-level singleton. Both OfflineProvider and new-round-client.tsx call getSyncEngine() independently, but because the constructor's window 'online'/'offline' listeners (lines 200-205) and start()'s interval creation (lines 214-227, guarded by if (this.syncIntervalId) return) only run once per singleton, no duplicate timers/listeners are created regardless of call-site count.
proposed_fix: None needed; cited as the reuse target for A11-001's proposed fix.

user_consequence: Low currently — this rule's live blast radius is legacy/admin surfaces, not the primary mobile dashboard. Recorded because it is the exact named anti-pattern the plan warns against, so it should not silently persist if a future change widens .card's consumers.
mechanism: src/app/globals.css:732-737 defines .card { ...; transform: translateZ(0); /* Force GPU layer */ ...} — an unconditional, permanent compositing-layer hint. Checked actual mounted consumers: the canonical modern surface primitive (src/components/ui/card.tsx, the Wave W2B consolidated Card used across the Fairway mobile dashboard) does NOT reference the .card class at all. Live .tsx consumers of the literal .card class are mostly src/app/golf/admin/crm/** and src/app/golf/join/** (legacy/admin/onboarding), not the primary player/coach dashboard screens in scope.
expected: No blanket compositing-layer promotion on a widely-shared utility class.
actual: Present, but current live consumers are legacy/admin, not the in-scope mobile dashboard.
proposed_fix: Confirm .card's remaining consumers before deprecating it as part of the broader primitive consolidation already underway; do not carry translateZ(0) forward into the canonical primitive.

user_consequence: A persistently-mounted, large-radius backdrop-filter blur (not a transient overlay) costs compositing work on every frame the surface is visible/scrolling, on top of whatever else the screen is doing. Not measured this phase, but the shape is real: this container is the main scrollable Calendar body, not a modal/sheet that appears briefly.
mechanism: src/components/golf/calendar/PremiumCalendarClient.tsx applies an inline style with backdropFilter:'blur(24px)' / WebkitBackdropFilter:'blur(24px)' to the 'Premium Glass Calendar Container' (around line 1141), wrapping the entire calendar's visible content, mounted for as long as Calendar is open. Repo-wide, 32 files reference backdrop-filter and ~25 call sites use a 20-40px blur radius, so this is a systemic pattern, not a one-off.
expected: Bounded/scoped glass material per C08, reserved for overlays/chrome, not a persistent full-height reading/scrolling surface.
actual: A 24px backdrop-filter blur is applied to the persistent main content container.
proposed_fix: Routed to A03 for the material recipe decision; A11 flags cost only.
performance_check: NOT_RUN — requires a release-build frame-timing profile with/without the blur (T25).
